installation_contract.validation: official controller and independently authenticated backend adapter

enforcement.before: Eight admission commands; installation manifest 3; configuration validation was in-process only and path checks matched a textual UID segment.
enforcement.after: Eight admission commands and their decision/exit meanings remain unchanged. Administrative validate-configuration adds format-1 request/response with exit 0 valid, 2 invalid, 4 malformed/error; no effect permission. Manifest 4 and lossless shared-default bootstrap format 7 require reconciled installation readers, resolved owned path observations and a plan/revision/source-bound validation receipt before registration. Strict installation readers need an adapter update.
enforcement.rationale: R26 exposes configuration checks without changing admission semantics. Trusted adapters supply authenticated current path facts and revalidate exact plans inside conditional registration; templates provide transport, not authority or installed dispatch certification.

delivery: Abstract interoperable contract; native/local interfaces suffice. No mandatory Node, MCP, CEL or hosted service.

evidence.authority: A supplied fact requires independent attributable scope-bound evidence; shape or a true boolean is not proof.

checkpoints.cardinality: One authoritative logical current adoption checkpoint per initialized workspace/persistent-runtime key; zero before initialization, no competing current authority.
checkpoints.discovery: Resolve authorized topology mapping before adoption discovery or creation; unknown ownership blocks dependent scope, never creates a session-derived fallback.
checkpoints.write: Use applicable expected-revision/concurrency and atomic persistence; atomic rename alone does not prevent lost updates.
checkpoints.reuse: Require exact relevant dependencies and current ownership/freshness; workspace switch invalidates active project state.
